text:
inga: Hey folks — customer reported streaming stops after ~30s when using EventSource in their browser. Works fine in curl. They're on Cloudflare in front of our Private deployment. Noticed partial output (first few events) then connection closes. :frowning:

maria-support: Thanks, @inga. Do we have a request id / sample client URL? Any repro steps from the customer?

inga: They sent a minimal repro. URL: https://stream.example-corp.com/sse?session=abc123 (proxy -> Cloudflare -> our edge). Client: Safari 15 on macOS and also Blink-based browsers using eventsource-polyfill. They said using curl keeps stream open.

sam-frontend: Common culprits: CDN buffering, wrong cache headers, or polyfill switching to XHR which triggers CORS preflight behavior. Do we know if their polyfill uses XHR fallback?

inga: They mentioned eventsource-polyfill v1.0.0 — which will fall back to XHR if server returns non-200/headers it expects. But logs show 200 from origin.

ops_jordan: Can we get response headers from the browser network tab or from curl? Need to check Transfer-Encoding and Cache-Control.

inga: Customer pasted curl -v output (sanitized):

> GET /sse?session=abc123 HTTP/1.1
> Host: stream.example-corp.com
> Accept: text/event-stream
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< cf-cache-status: HIT
< Content-Length: 

inga: They highlighted cf-cache-status: HIT. :thinking:

sam-frontend: A CDN HIT is a red flag — SSE must be unbuffered. If Cloudflare is caching or buffering the origin response, it may close the connection or deliver only buffered bytes. Also Cache-Control: private doesn't make sense for SSE.

maria-support: We should confirm how our Private deployment sets cache headers for streaming routes. @eng-runtime or @eng-platform any idea?

nate-runtime: Runtime always sets Content-Type: text/event-stream and removes Content-Length. We set Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, private by default for streaming endpoints, but platform may override.

ops_jordan: If Cloudflare is seeing the response as cacheable (HIT), something upstream is setting a cacheable header. Could be an intermediary or the customer's origin (their edge) modifying headers. Does the request have any query string auth token? If token in URL then CDN may cache per-token which is bad.

inga: They do pass session token in query param for EventSource since the browser EventSource can't set Authorization header. So URL is /sse?session=abc123. Customer said they rotate tokens every minute.

sam-frontend: Token-in-URL + CDN can cause cached SSE responses which then serve static content and close. Also some CDNs will strip Transfer-Encoding chunked and buffer. Safari will close if it never sees a newline-separated event. Polyfills may use XHR and get blocked by CORS if Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing.

ops_jordan: Can we ask for a HAR or full response header dump? Also need Cloudflare upstream logs — whether it mutated cache-control.

inga: Asked customer, they returned additional header dump from Cloudflare trace: cf-cache-status: HIT, cf-cache-tier: edge, response headers included: Cache-Control: max-age=60, vary: Accept-Encoding

maria-support: There's the problem: Cache-Control: max-age=60. Origin must be sending something cacheable or Cloudflare is configured to cache by path. If Cloudflare serves cached response it will close connection after delivering buffered body — SSE won't reconnect properly.

sam-frontend: Short-term mitigation: advise customer to set cache-busting query param unique per client (but they already rotate token), and ensure Cloudflare rule to bypass cache for /sse path or set Origin Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache and Cache-Control: private, no-transform. Also ensure Cache-Control: no-transform so intermediate proxies don't modify chunking.

inga: Customer tried bypassing cache via page rule and saw improvement — stream stayed open longer but still saw occasional single-event truncation. They captured browser console showing "EventSource failed to connect: 200 OK but no events" and eventsource-polyfill logs switching to XHR:

[polyfill] using XHR fallback — CORS preflight required

maria-support: When polyfill uses XHR fallback it will do OPTIONS preflight which must return CORS headers. Browser EventSource does a GET without custom headers so no preflight normally.

sam-frontend: We should provide recommended headers to the customer. Minimal for SSE:
- Content-Type: text/event-stream
- Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
- Connection: keep-alive
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length)
- Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <their origin> or * (for dev)
- Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Last-Event-ID (optional)

nate-runtime: Also recommend disabling any CDN caching for SSE endpoints and adding Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate; or Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, max-age=0.

ops_jordan: Another angle: some CDNs will only stream from origin if "Origin" header matches; otherwise they will cache. Check Cloudflare worker rules or page rules that might treat query strings less precisely.

inga: Customer also mentioned they see intermittent 304 responses from edge to origin, and a 304 back to the client within a few seconds. That could be due to conditional GET from CF, which is a problem for streaming — 304 has no body.

sam-frontend: 304 => no body => EventSource gets no data and may close. So we must ensure CDN doesn't revalidate streaming paths.

maria-support: Can we reproduce ourselves? @sam-frontend @nate-runtime can one of you spin a public test hostname through Cloudflare and simulate SSE with caching rules on?

sam-frontend: I can try a quick repro with a small node server and Cloudflare dev mode off. Will report back.

--- 18 minutes later ---

sam-frontend: Repro complete. With Cloudflare caching enabled on path, EventSource connection receives initial buffered chunk then CF closes connection. curl still shows whole buffered payload. When I force CF bypass, stream stays open.

sam-frontend: Also tried polyfill — once buffer delivered then XHR fallback received full buffered response and polyfill didn't stream incremental events.

maria-support: Ok, action items for customer:
1) Disable caching for /sse endpoints on their CDN (Page Rule or Worker). Ensure CF returns cf-cache-status: BYPASS or MISS.
2) Set Origin/Server headers: "Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, private, max-age=0" and "Connection: keep-alive" and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
3) Prefer using server-sent tokens in cookie with samesite if possible, or short-lived query token but ensure CDN bypasses cache.
4) If using polyfill, ensure CORS headers are present for OPTIONS and that server returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin + Access-Control-Allow-Methods + Access-Control-Allow-Headers expected by polyfill.

inga: Customer applied Page Rule to bypass cache for /sse/* and updated server headers. They say streaming looks stable in Chrome. Safari still shows occasional reconnection after ~45s with a "Network error".

sam-frontend: Safari is picky. Ensure there are periodic keepalive comments to prevent idle close:

: keepalive

Send a comment or a ping event every 15-20s to keep connection alive. Also double-check TLS session timeouts on their edge and Cloudflare idle timeouts.

nate-runtime: We also noticed our runtime emits a ": ping" every 30s by default; if Cloudflare buffers, pings get dropped. With bypass, pings arrive.

maria-support: Good. I'll send a concise troubleshooting note to the customer with the steps + header sample and ask for Cloudflare cache status and a HAR after changes. Thanks everyone. :+1:

support-bot: Escalation ticket created: #ES-4421, assigned to eng-platform for follow-up on default cache headers for private deployments.

ops_jordan: I'll add a checklist for Private deployment docs to explicitly call out SSE headers and recommended Cloudflare settings.

inga: Customer verified 24h stability after applying bypass + keepalive. Closing from customer side. They may follow up about moving to cookie-based auth. :tada:

maria-support: Resolving thread — will attach our header snippets and CF page rule examples to the support ticket.
